nodes.label: Deliberately Duplicated audit.py With Divergent Signatures
nodes.norm_label: deliberately duplicated audit.py with divergent signatures

nodes.label: Decision 1: LangGraph, archive the other two variants
nodes.norm_label: decision 1: langgraph, archive the other two variants
nodes.rationale: Only architecture with a genuine durable interrupt — interrupt() plus a checkpointer. The AgentExecutor and RunnablePipeline variants cannot pause across process death at all.

nodes.label: Dependency Note: AgentExecutor vs LangGraph Contrast Is Gone
nodes.norm_label: dependency note: agentexecutor vs langgraph contrast is gone
nodes.rationale: AgentExecutor left langchain.agents in langchain 1.0 and langchain>=0.2.0 now resolves to 1.4.x, where create_agent is LangGraph underneath. The contrast the three variants existed to demonstrate no longer exists — the substantive argument for archiving them as history.

nodes.label: archive/ — Retired Variants
nodes.rationale: The three-architecture comparison stopped being meaningful: AgentExecutor left langchain.agents in langchain 1.0 and on 1.x `create_agent` is LangGraph underneath, so the contrast no longer exists. Kept as working history, not maintained.

nodes.label: scaffold_hitl_repo.py Overwrite Incident
nodes.rationale: The generator wrote every file with "w"; running it twice left main.py containing its own generator, a duplicated [project] table, and an unterminated fence. Lesson recorded: any regenerator must refuse to overwrite existing files.

nodes.label: decide
nodes.rationale: The single place the escalate-only invariant is expressed: gate = tier_requires_gate OR confidence_requires_gate, with deliberately no branch where high confidence sets gate False.

nodes.label: estimate_confidence
nodes.rationale: Rule-based ambiguity marker count, deliberately kept as only a confidence signal and never a substitute for the tier; structured LLM output is a later upgrade.

nodes.label: risk_tier
nodes.rationale: Tier comes from the action, never the wording; unknown action kinds fail closed at "high" so an unrecognised verb cannot sail through.

nodes.label: No LLM Dependency
nodes.rationale: Confidence scoring is rule-based, so langchain-openai is explicitly forbidden — the project stays offline-testable and has no API key surface.

nodes.label: Confidence Signal
nodes.rationale: Independent second signal from request ambiguity, rule-based initially with structured LLM output as a later upgrade — it exists to escalate, not to authorise.

nodes.label: The Invariant (spec §6)
nodes.rationale: Confidence may only escalate to a gate, never clear one policy requires. A high confidence score on transition -> Done still pauses. This is the single property separating real HITL from HITL theater; it lives in one function and is asserted by one test.

nodes.label: Out Of Scope (spec §11)
nodes.rationale: Web UI, multi-approver quorum, notification/escalation and LLM-based confidence scoring are deferred — add when a second human must approve something, or when rule-based tiering demonstrably mis-tiers.

nodes.label: Policy Tier Table
nodes.rationale: Deterministic tier derived from the action, never the prose: transition to a terminal state is high, create_issue medium, transition between open states and add_comment low.

nodes.label: Known Limitation: Self-Asserted Identity (spec §10)
nodes.rationale: `--as <human_id>` has no authentication; honest for a local single-operator tool, a hole under real compliance weight. Ships with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling and the upgrade path (OS user + signed approval token).

nodes.label: UNCERTAINTY_MARKERS Keyword Grep (rejected detector)
nodes.rationale: `any(m in text.lower() for m in UNCERTAINTY_MARKERS)` is a keyword grep, not a confidence estimate: "I am definitely not sure" and "the Unknown Pleasures album" both trip it, while a confidently-worded destructive request passes clean. Replaced by two independent signals.

nodes.label: Durable Approval Step
nodes.rationale: A pending approval is a row on disk, not a thread parked in memory, so it survives a crash, a reboot, or an approver who is asleep. The process is allowed to exit at the gate rather than block.

nodes.label: Escalate-Only Confidence Invariant
nodes.rationale: Risk tier is derived from the action (`transition -> Done` is high, always), never from how confidently the request was worded. Confidence may only escalate to a gate, never clear one. That single rule is the difference between human-in-the-loop and human-in-the-loop theater.

nodes.label: Self-Asserted Approver Identity
nodes.rationale: `approve --as <human_id>` has no authentication. Honest for a local single-operator tool, a real hole for anything carrying compliance weight. Upgrade path: OS user + signed approval token.

nodes.label: FakeJira
nodes.rationale: Records every call so tests can assert nothing ran on deny, and takes fail_with so the post-approval failure path is exercisable without a network.

nodes.label: JiraPort (Protocol)
nodes.rationale: runtime_checkable Protocol so the graph is written and tested against an interface; binding the real API later touches exactly one class.

nodes.label: RovoJira
nodes.rationale: Stub that raises JiraError pointing at Task 7; maps onto createJiraIssue, transitionJiraIssue (via getTransitionsForJiraIssue) and addCommentToJiraIssue, all of which require cloudId. Transition resolves status name to transition ID per call; cache per project only if latency demands.

nodes.label: Commit The Repaired State
nodes.rationale: The scaffold is gone but every repair exists only as untracked working-tree files; a second accidental deletion would take all of it, exactly as it took the scaffold. Hence "commit first" as prerequisite.

nodes.label: Decision 4: Build behind JiraPort, bind the live API last
nodes.norm_label: decision 4: build behind jiraport, bind the live api last
nodes.rationale: Jira is currently unreachable, but the port is correct design regardless — the whole graph stays buildable and testable with no network.

nodes.label: Flatten The Layout
nodes.rationale: The doubly-nested directory collapses to a conventional src/ layout, and a root pyproject.toml with [tool.pytest.ini_options] opts the project into make test-all, which scripts/run-tests.sh currently skips for lack of a top-level pyproject.

nodes.label: Known Blocker: Jira Is Unreachable
nodes.rationale: The Atlassian account authenticates but getAccessibleAtlassianResources() returns []; every Jira tool needs a cloudId and there is no site to obtain one from. Cause is no provisioned Jira Cloud site or a connector authorized without site scope — resolved by the user, not this project.

nodes.label: Jira Not Yet Bound
nodes.rationale: `getAccessibleAtlassianResources()` returns `[]`, so there is no cloudId to call any Jira tool with. Building against JiraPort with FakeJira keeps the whole graph complete and tested without a network; binding the live API is one class.

nodes.label: build_graph
nodes.rationale: Nodes are closures over the injected JiraPort, so the same graph shape is used in tests and in the CLI with different backends.

nodes.label: State (TypedDict)
nodes.rationale: `audits` is Annotated[list[dict], operator.add] so every node appends to one accumulating trail instead of overwriting it; state.py folds into graph.py because it is one TypedDict.

nodes.label: Decision 3: Async + durable approval
nodes.rationale: The agent exits at the gate and a separate CLI resumes from a checkpoint in a fresh process, keyed by thread_id = request_id.

nodes.label: Decision 2: Gate Jira issue create / transition
nodes.norm_label: decision 2: gate jira issue create / transition
nodes.rationale: Real integration that is reversible, so the full execute path can be exercised safely. Gmail was considered and rejected because sending mail is irreversible, which would have forced a permanent draft-only mode and left the execute path untested.

nodes.label: Denial Executes Nothing
nodes.rationale: Denied is a terminal state with actions_taken: []; FakeJira records calls precisely so a test can prove nothing ran.

nodes.label: Four Load-Bearing Tests (spec §9)
nodes.rationale: Policy floor cannot be bypassed by high confidence; interrupt survives a new process (a fresh checkpointer instance, not the same object in memory); request_id is stable across every stage; denial executes nothing.

nodes.label: No Auto-Retry After Approved Execution Fails
nodes.norm_label: no auto-retry after approved execution fails
nodes.rationale: A retry is a new approval cycle. Silently re-running an approved side effect is how duplicate writes happen; the audit records final_decision "failed" instead.

nodes.label: checkpointer_for
nodes.rationale: Wraps SqliteSaver.from_conn_string (itself a context manager) so callers need not know that, and so the parent directory is created.

nodes.label: main (hitl CLI)
nodes.rationale: thread_id is the request_id, so approve/deny in a fresh process address the exact paused run; --seed exists only so FakeJira has issues to act on until RovoJira is bound.

nodes.label: make_audit
nodes.rationale: Keyword-only because positional order is a footgun for a ten-field audit record; request_id is a parameter, never minted inside, so one request's stages correlate.

nodes.label: Fixed Audit JSON Schema
nodes.rationale: Exactly ten keys, fixed by the operating spec, so a trail written by any stage is replayable and diffable; append-only JSONL at audit/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.

nodes.label: Verified LangGraph API (Do Not Substitute From Memory)
nodes.norm_label: verified langgraph api (do not substitute from memory)
nodes.rationale: Pinned facts because recalled APIs are wrong here: interrupt/Command come from langgraph.types, SqliteSaver from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite, from_conn_string is a context manager not a constructor, and a paused invoke returns a dict containing __interrupt__.

nodes.label: Audit Trail (spec §7)
nodes.rationale: One make_audit, one fixed key set, append-only JSONL at audit/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl so the trail can be replayed from disk.

nodes.label: Defect: datetime.utcnow() naive timestamps
nodes.rationale: Deprecated and returns a naive timestamp, which is wrong for an audit log. Use datetime.now(timezone.utc).

nodes.label: Defect: request_id minted per make_audit call
nodes.norm_label: defect: request_id minted per make_audit call
nodes.rationale: Every stage of one request got a different ID, so the trail cannot be correlated and the audit requirement is structurally unmet. Fix: mint once at submit and thread through.

nodes.label: SQLite Checkpointer
nodes.rationale: State must be persisted outside the process so a later `approve` in a brand new process can resume the same graph run.

nodes.label: Three-Process Approval Cycle
nodes.rationale: submit / approve / audit are three separate process invocations on purpose — that is the demonstration that the pause is durable rather than an in-memory wait.
